scenario: A remote worker in a thin-walled apartment spends most of the day on calls and needs to replace or quiet a disruptive clicky keyboard without accepting a soft or unreliable feel. The investigation must audit the exact Mistel X-VIII Cherry MX Silent Red offer, compare two tightly scoped damping experiences, trace noise from switch source to microphone and wall observer, and decide what can be tried without pretending that membrane-equivalent quietness has already been measured.
target: Distinguish the exact Mistel offer and its seller acoustic claim from independent performance, compare the direct but different-switch and different-mod experiences without treating either as O-ring or Mistel evidence, explain why switch damping alone cannot establish call-microphone or through-wall behavior, and make a conditional keep, return, nonmechanical, or defer recommendation using a reproducible real-room trial. State explicitly that the evidence does not establish membrane-equivalent quietness.
